verdicts.reason: Version A splits each field's rules into small, single-purpose functions (passwordError, usernameError, referralError, ageOn, minAge) and keeps validateSignup a flat, uniform list of calls, which makes each rule easy to find, test and change; Version B inlines password, username and referral logic into the main function and packs parsing, date validation, age calculation and per-country rules into one birthDateError, although its step-by-step email checks are more readable than A's lookaround regexes.

B splits each rule into small, named, single-purpose functions (passwordError, usernameError, ageOn, minAge, referralError), so each rule can be read, tested and changed in isolation, whereas A puts password, username and referral logic inline in validateSignup; B's dense lookaround email regexes are the one place where A's explicit step-by-step checks read better.
